docker build  -t bun-version . --progress=plain

In my case, perhaps similar to @participant9, it happens only with `--production`.

(And it doesn't happen, unsurprisingly, when the install cache is already populated.)

Of course, like others have mentioned above, installing the production set only means that a different set of dependencies gets installed which could be the real issue.

Locally on my M1 Mac that works:
```bash
bun install v1.0.18 (36c316a2)
 + ts-typed-events@3.0.0
```

In a container running via Colima on the same system:
```bash
bun install v1.0.18 (36c316a2)
[20.69ms] migrated lockfile from package-lock.json
  🚚 typescript... error: IntegrityCheckFailed extracting tarball for typescript + ts-typed-events@3.0.0
[224.00ms] done
```
Not sure if the `typescript +` part has something to do with it?

If I first change to a temporary directory and do `bun install ts-typed-events@3.0.0` (populating the install cache) and then switch back to repeat the package install, then everything works fine.

comments.body:
I was also running into this issue and the fix was simple in my case, but it may not apply to everyone.

You need to ignore the `node_modules` folder in a `.dockerignore`:

```shell
# Dependencies
**/node_modules
```

This happens because you are sending your `Windows` dependency installations into a different `Linux` environment (the container) where it **rightfully** complains that the versions of the packages it is downloading don't match the existing `Windows` ones (IntegrityCheck). This is why it was hard to reproduce, you need to test with a package that has different installations for each OS.

Also, note that the way `.dockerignore` works is on a per context basis, so you need to create one in each folder where you copy things to your docker images. I was working on a monorepo and had a `.dockerignore` in my `api` folder but not in the root of the repository where the `node_modules` folder was being created so I still got this error.

If you're running into this in pure GitHub actions (without Docker), then you may not be correctly ignoring `node_modules` in your repository `.gitignore`, which you should be doing from the start.

I think this issue can now be closed.
